session_4.result:
I added both commands, and the full suite passes (15 tests, including 3 new ones). The work is committed as `bfc557a`.

- **`dedupe`**: for each set of tasks with exactly the same title (case-sensitive), it keeps the one with the earliest `due_at` and deletes the rest. It prints how many it removed. If due dates tie, the first one in the file is kept. The logic is `dedupe_tasks()` in `tinytasks/api.py`.
- **`copy ID`**: it creates `"<title> (copy)"` with the same `due_at` as the original and prints it in the same format as `add`. If the ID doesn't exist, it prints `no such task`. The logic is `copy_task()` in `tinytasks/api.py`. The copy isn't archived, even if the original was.

`dedupe` treats archived tasks like any other. If an archived task has the earliest `due_at` among duplicates, it's kept and the active ones are removed. I followed your spec literally here. Tell me if you'd rather it ignore archived tasks.

Git warned that LF line endings in two files will become CRLF the next time Git touches them. That's only a line-ending setting on Windows and doesn't change the code.
